proposed.text: Trap #46 addresses vertical clearance for accessible parking. What minimum vertical clearance must accessible parking spaces provide, and why does this differ from standard parking clearance?

options.text: 2100 mm minimum — the same as standard parking, since accessible spaces do not require additional clearance
2200 mm minimum — 100 mm more than standard parking, to allow a person standing beside the car to open the door fully
2300 mm minimum — required exclusively for accessible spaces to accommodate raised-roof vans
2500 mm minimum — providing generous clearance for all vehicle types used by PWDs, including high-roof vans

proposed.rationale: Trap #46: accessible parking requires 2300 mm minimum vertical clearance — exclusively for raised-roof vans. Trap #46 in the article. Standard parking structures typically provide 2100–2200 mm vertical clearance. BP 344 IRR requires a minimum of 2300 mm vertical clearance specifically at accessible parking spaces to accommodate raised-roof vans (wheelchair-accessible vehicles with elevated rooflines). This is not required throughout the entire parking structure — only at the accessible spaces. An accessible parking level at 2100 mm standard clearance would physically prevent raised-roof van access to the only spaces intended for the users who need them most.
proposed.explanation: Accessible parking: 2300 mm min vertical clearance (vs. standard 2100 mm) — raised-roof vans require the additional headroom.
